note: Market sentiment & global flows for the overview. Fear&Greed is fetched LIVE in-browser (CNN equity index via proxy + crypto via alternative.me) with the baked value as fallback; breadth & regional flows are researched and baked (no free real-time API) and refreshed daily by the scheduled intel agent.

components.name: Market Momentum
components.reading: S&P 500 vs its 125-day moving average. The index closed 7 July at 7,503.85, comfortably above a rising 125-day average and within ~1.5% of its record — momentum has firmed to the constructive side even after the 7 July semiconductor pullback.

components.name: Stock Price Strength
components.reading: Net 52-week highs vs lows on the NYSE. Net new highs stayed positive as breadth broadened through late June/early July (~66.6% of the S&P above its 200-DMA), but the 7 July chip-led session narrowed the reading back toward neutral.

components.name: Stock Price Breadth
components.reading: McClellan Volume Summation (advancing vs declining volume). The Summation Index has been grinding higher on broadening participation, but the 7 July semis rout (Samsung earnings, DeepSeek fears) rolled the short-term McClellan Oscillator back toward neutral/negative.

components.name: Put/Call Options
components.reading: 5-day put/call ratio. Options buyers stayed defensive into the 8 July June FOMC minutes and the 14 July June CPI print, keeping the 5-day ratio tilted toward puts despite the calm VIX.

components.name: Market Volatility
components.reading: VIX vs its 50-day moving average. The VIX sat at ~15.6 on 7 July — well below its 50-day average and near the low end of its recent range, a decidedly non-fearful read even amid the tech wobble.

components.name: Safe-Haven Demand
components.reading: 20-day stock vs Treasury bond return spread. Equities outpaced Treasuries over the trailing window as the 10-year backed up to 4.50% (a two-week high on firmer oil and hawkish-Fed repricing), so stocks-over-bonds performance nudges this toward neutral rather than fear.

components.name: Junk Bond Demand
components.reading: Yield spread between junk bonds and investment-grade. HY OAS remains historically tight, but put-heavy HY hedging and a still-cautious credit bid keep demand for risky credit only lukewarm.

metrics.label: % of S&P 500 stocks above 200-day MA
metrics.value: ~66.6% (Barchart $S5TH, 7 July; 52-week range 42.1-68.6, near the top of the range) — a firmly constructive, above-half reading

metrics.label: % of S&P 500 stocks above 50-day MA
metrics.value: ~67.4% (Barchart $S5FI, 7 July; flagged 'strong buy', 52-week range 17.7-75.5) — broad short-term participation

metrics.label: NYSE advancers vs decliners (latest session)
metrics.value: Decliners led on the 7 July semis-driven down session (~44% advancers, approximate); a weaker internal than late-June's advancer-led tape

metrics.label: 52-week New Highs minus New Lows (NYSE)
metrics.value: Net positive but narrowing as chip weakness on 7 July trimmed new highs; precise live counts not extractable from JS-rendered tables (approximate)

metrics.label: NYSE McClellan Oscillator / Summation Index
metrics.value: Summation Index has trended higher on broadening breadth since mid-May, but the short-term Oscillator rolled toward neutral/negative on the 7 July tech rout (mcoscillator.com; exact daily NYMO not published in accessible sources; approximate)

metrics.label: Cumulative NYSE Advance-Decline line trend
metrics.value: Rising and near highs — the broad A-D line continues to confirm the tape, a healthier picture than the narrow mega-cap-only leadership of earlier in 2026 (approximate trend read)

metrics.label: % of 11 S&P sectors above their 200-DMA
metrics.value: ~73-82% (roughly 8-9 of 11 sector ETFs) as leadership stayed broad across Financials, Industrials, Health Care and Utilities; consistent with the ~66% S5TH reading (inferred)

breadth.note: Breadth remains broad and constructive into early July: ~66.6% of the S&P sits above its 200-DMA and ~67.4% above the 50-DMA, both near the top of their 52-week ranges, with the cumulative A-D line near highs and 8-9 of 11 sectors above trend. The one soft spot is a 7 July semiconductor-led down session (weak Samsung earnings and renewed DeepSeek efficiency fears) that rolled the short-term McClellan Oscillator toward neutral — the open question is whether the 8 July June FOMC minutes and the 14 July June CPI print let the broadening continue or re-narrow the tape around a hawkish Fed.

flows.period: Freshest fully-itemized week: week ending 24 June 2026 (BofA 'Flow Show' and ICI, both reporting the June 24 week). A newer EPFR Global Navigator ('Bond Fund flows maintain record pace', published 7 July, covering the week to ~1 July) confirms the same bonds-leading theme, but its itemized regional figures are paywalled and are NOT baked here. Flows are weekly and lagged.
flows.narrative: The dominant story flipped from June's US-concentration surge into a rotation OUT of crowded mega-cap AI/tech and into duration, real assets and hedges. In the week to 24 June, tech funds saw a record weekly outflow (-$9.3B) and US equities their first outflow in 13 weeks (-$8.5B), while money-market/cash funds shed -$25.5B — money leaving parked cash but going into bonds (+$16.6B, a 61st straight inflow week), gold (+$3.5B, a 6-week high), and rate-sensitive corners (REITs, infrastructure) rather than back into US tech. BofA's Bull & Bear Indicator sits at ~9.1, deep in 'extreme greed'/contrarian-sell territory.

regions.note: First US-equity fund outflow in 13 weeks (BofA); ICI corroborates with domestic-equity mutual funds -$18.1B and total equity -$13.9B for the same week. Tech was the epicenter at a record -$9.3B.
No clean single-week figure in public sources; 2026 YTD skew stays pro-international (~$104B to intl-DM vs ~$25B US per BofA). Weekly direction modest inflow, approximate.
EM equity funds broadly positive in June, led by Asia-ex-Japan (Taiwan, Korea). Exact June-24-week figure not public — approximate.
Mainland-China equity funds posting outflows as authorities cap the rally; China bond funds on a multi-week inflow streak. Specific weekly figure not public — approximate.
No verifiable standalone figure for this week in public sources; direction unconfirmed.
Biggest cash outflow in 8 weeks — parked cash being redeployed, but into duration and hedges rather than back into crowded US equities.

61st consecutive week of bond inflows; Treasuries +$5.3B (10th straight week). ICI (mutual-fund only) shows taxable bonds +$3.9B, munis +$0.85B. The 7 July EPFR headline confirms bonds still setting a record pace.
Biggest gold inflow in 6 weeks as Hartnett explicitly favored gold over USD exposure — a reversal from the prior weeks' gold-fund bleed, tracking gold's steadying near $4,150.

movements.note: The marquee rotation — record tech outflow with liquidity moving to rate-sensitive and real-asset cyclicals; Real Estate/REITs +$0.9B (biggest since Mar-2024), Infrastructure +$1.5B (most in 6 weeks).
Investors left parked cash for duration; Treasuries +$5.3B in a 10th straight inflow week as the soft jobs print skewed the next rate move lower.
A persistent pro-international/EM tilt reasserted itself after 13 weeks of US concentration; 2026 YTD international-DM inflows (~$104B) still dwarf US (~$25B).
Gold explicitly favored over the dollar as a hedge; a clean reversal of the prior weeks' gold-fund outflows.
Energy funds saw their biggest outflow since Apr-2025 as crude slid, while AI-power/infrastructure funds drew their most in six weeks.
